symptom: ako/mxcli#1982 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1751): a merge conflicting on a text file and the model: `git merge` stopped on the text file, the human resolved and staged it, the re-run hit ManualResolutionRequired (exit 2) and aborted — and `git merge --abort` reset the index with the resolution in it. `--plan` then re-merged, met the text conflict unresolved, wrote the model, repaired the hashes and failed at the commit with 'Committing is not possible because you have unmerged files': half done, the resolution gone.
cause: The exit-2 path aborts with `git merge --abort` and recorded nothing about the index; applyPlan never looked for non-model conflicts (only mergeRun did), so it went straight to the engine and the model write.
file: cmd/mxcli/cmd_git_merge_text.go (stagedTextResolutions / restoreTextResolutions / openTextConflicts), cmd/mxcli/cmd_git_merge.go (exit-2 path records the resolutions in the plan template's `resolved`; applyPlan restores them onto paths that conflict again, then stops on any open text conflict before the stale check, the engine and the model)
insight: An abort that resets the index is a data-loss step for whatever the human staged, so record it before aborting — and the index blob of a staged path is already in the object store, which `merge --abort` does not prune, so the plan template only needs path + blob (or deleted). Restoring only onto a path that conflicts again leaves a cleanly merged one as the merge made it. The fake engine (engineDecides) and real git make the reporter's three steps a unit test; the first run reproduced the exact 'unmerged files' commit error. Revert proofs: with the restore stubbed, the open-conflict check now stops the plan safely (resolution lost but nothing half-written); with the check stubbed, the engine runs with the text conflict open. Real-mx integration tests (11.12.6) still pass.
